newsitem.title: USA: USDA seeks longer livestock disaster aid - Glickman.
newsitem.headline: USDA seeks longer livestock disaster aid - Glickman.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department was seeking ways to prolong disaster aid to blizzard-stricken ranchers, Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Tuesday. Glickman also moved to clarify who is eligible for feed assistance.

Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle, South Dakota Democrat, said he planned to file legislation later this week to exempt ranchers from capital gains taxes if they are forced to sell livestock, so long as they buy more stock later.
Glickman told reporters that about $40 million was available for disaster aid at present. He said he would like to make aid available through the worst of the winter season.
"We will use the fund to help them (ranchers) and their problems," Glickman said following a meeting with Daschle and Senator Byron Dorgan, North Dakota Democrat.
The senators said it probably would become necessary to ask Congress for more money.

"This is a catastropic disaster," Glickman said, referring to blizzards that repeatedly have struck the northern Plains. There were estimates 50,000 cattle have died in North Dakota and South Dakota from the storms and lack of feed.

Glickman said the Agriculture Department had clarified its rules on eligibility for aid. In brief, ranchers may be eligible if their stock was in danger because they they did not have access to normal feed supplies. USDA aid would help pay for substitute feed or for snow removal January 10-25.
USDA was "looking for ways to provide additional assistance," perhaps for another 30 days, Glickman said.
"In my judgement, we ought to expand it to get through the heart...of the winter feeding season."
Dorgan said ranchers in his state "face a crisis out there trying to get feed to livestock."
Daschle complimented USDA for being innovative in furnishing aid.
"We're asking for additional snow days to make eligibility last longer," Daschle said.
